name: ai-maestro-visual-communicator-plugin
description: Generate interactive HTML pages — diagrams, diff reviews, plan reviews, slide decks, data tables, and v2 modal-comment agent reports. Every page sends the user's selection (or per-element comment thread) back to the agent.

cpv._intentional_validator_false_positives_r: Documented validator false-positives. Each entry is a per-finding allowlist of (file, level, message_substring) consumed by publish.py::_gate_validate(). FOUR SOURCE BANDS: (A) skills/amvcp-self-debug-rules/SKILL.md bare-slug-path WARNINGs (upstream bug #30 candidate) — bullet-list slugs that ARE valid sibling skills but the bare-slug heuristic doesn't walk the plugin's skills/ tree. (B) skills/amvcp-wireframe/SKILL.md MAJOR `Reference to non-existent skill 'amvcp-wf` (upstream bug #27) — the HEAD-list parser sees the bullet-list prefix `amvcp-wf-` as an empty-suffix entry. (C) `<skillaudit-native>` install-integrity (upstream bug #32 candidate) — CPV's bundled scanner cannot locate its own rules/skillaudit_patterns.json inside the uvx-cached site-packages. (D) CPV-SOURCE FILES BUNDLED INSIDE PLUGIN (new in v1.3.5+) — `scripts/skillaudit_patterns.json`, `scripts/cpv_skillaudit_rules.py`, `scripts/scan-for-prompt-injection.py`, `scripts/render-skill-audit.py`, `scripts/cpv_network_resilience.py` are mirrors of CPV's own skill-auditor source code that we ship inside our scripts/ so the user's local skill-auditor can run without a separate CPV install. CPV is now scanning ITS OWN regex catalog and detection rules and emitting ~221+ skillaudit findings on every pattern that matches its own pattern descriptions. This is the recursive-self-scan FP (upstream bug #42, FILED 2026-05-23 — supersedes the earlier '#38 candidate' label; #38 was CLOSED for the doc-prose subset, #42 covers the scanner's own catalog/rule-source shipped in scripts/). The 5 files MUST be allowlisted wholesale (every skillaudit:* family). (E) VENDORED COMPILED JS BUNDLES — `scripts/amvcp-runtime.js`, `scripts/amvcp-tokens.js`, `scripts/amvcp-diagram.js`, `scripts/amvcp-chart.js`, `scripts/amvcp-form-inputs.js`, `scripts/amvcp-tables.js`, `scripts/amvcp-token-sheet.js`, `scripts/amvcp-interactive.js`, `scripts/amvcp-code-highlight.js`, `scripts/amvcp-designmd.js`, `scripts/amvcp-regex.umd.js`, `scripts/amvcp-slide.js`, `scripts/amvcp-pierre-diff.mjs` are pre-built minified browser bundles. Their skillaudit findings are the same over-fire class as band D (CPV's matcher hitting compiled browser bundles that ship no executable plugin code) and are tracked under the same upstream bug #42; any source-level fix would require upstream vendor changes, not plugin edits. (F) USER-DECLARED INTENTIONAL-DRIFT runtime files — `scripts/render-interactive-report.py`, `scripts/amvcp-show-launcher.py`, `scripts/amvcp-select.py`, `scripts/share.py`, `skills/amvcp-show/scripts/dispatch.py` — pre-approved by maintainer; their subprocess/network/encoding patterns are intentional. (G) IN-FILE DOCUMENTATION FPs — TOC text in skill markdowns and prose in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` rationale strings trip skillaudit pattern matchers; these are pure documentation. (H) RC-DATA-INSTALLER-001 WARNING — package.json declares NO runtime deps (only metadata), so a SessionStart installer is not needed; CPV's heuristic doesn't distinguish. The matcher in `_gate_validate()` allowlists findings whose (file, level) tuple matches and whose message CONTAINS the listed `message_substring`. Findings outside this allowlist still block G3 normally. ALL allowlisted entries cite the upstream bug they correspond to in the `upstream_bug` field — when CPV ships the fix, the entry can be removed.

_intentional_validator_false_positives.message_substring: SkillAudit native scan could not run
_intentional_validator_false_positives.rationale: CPV's bundled `cpv_skillaudit_native.py` resolves its rule catalog as `Path(__file__).parent.parent / 'rules' / 'skillaudit_patterns.json'`, but the `rules/` directory at the CPV repo top-level is NOT packaged as `package_data` in CPV's pyproject — so when CPV is installed via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/Emasoft/claude-plugins-validation`, the catalog is missing from the cached site-packages and the scanner cannot start. The catalog DOES exist in CPV's git checkout (~/.cache/uv/git-v0/checkouts/.../rules/skillaudit_patterns.json) but uv archives only the importable Python package, not sibling top-level dirs. Workarounds: (a) ship the patterns file inside the package, (b) make `_RULES_PATH` walk up to find a `rules/` sibling of the repo root, (c) bundle as `importlib.resources`. Until upstream ships any of those, the scanner returns a CRITICAL on every CPV invocation against any plugin — universal blast radius, not anything our plugin can cause or fix.

All 5 absolute-path findings (lines 144 /etc/, 144 /usr/, 174 /etc/shadow, 473 /etc/cron, 617 /etc/passwd) are LITERAL strings inside this file's JSON regex-pattern catalog — they are the patterns the skill-auditor scanner USES to detect malicious skills that reference sensitive Unix paths. They are NOT hardcoded absolute paths used by our runtime code (the file is loaded as opaque JSON data by `cpv_skillaudit_rules.py`). CPV's absolute-path lint should skip files whose basename matches `*_patterns*.json` / `*_rules*.json` (similar to how it skips lockfiles and vendor dirs). Single message_substring `"Absolute path found: '/"` matches all 5 findings.

Recursive self-scan FP — CPV is scanning its OWN regex pattern catalog and emitting CRITICAL findings on every pattern that matches its own pattern descriptions (privilege_escalation, crypto_theft, credential_theft, code_execution, agent_manipulation, prompt_injection, data_exfiltration, etc.). The file is opaque JSON data loaded by `cpv_skillaudit_rules.py` — NOT executable code. CPV's skill-auditor scanner must skip files whose basename matches `*_patterns*.json` (its own catalog) to avoid this O(N²) self-match. Single `[skillaudit:` substring matches every skillaudit:* finding regardless of subtype.

Line 329 contains a legitimate regex `text.replace(/^\uFEFF/, '')` that strips a leading UTF-8 BOM from input text — the BOM character itself is required as a regex literal. The skillaudit scanner flags the BOM as `Invisible character: Zero-width no-break space`, but the file's INTENT is to remove the BOM, not embed it covertly. This is the inverse of malicious — it's defensive.

Line 119 — bytes-literal `b'<title>Selection received \xe2\x80\x94 close this tab</title>'` where `\xe2\x80\x94` is the UTF-8 encoding of em-dash. The scanner flags non-ASCII bytes-literal encoding as OBFUSCATION but the intent is just to ship a precomposed HTML page (no runtime template parsing). User-approved intentional pattern.

Line 848 binds the local selection server to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — required for the Chromium `--app` window to fetch the selection page on the same host. The scanner flags `127.0.0.1` as SSRF; this is a legitimate loopback bind, not an SSRF vector (the server only listens on loopback, no outbound).

Same line 848 loopback `127.0.0.1` URL — already justified in the SSRF allowlist entry above. The URL_RAW_IP rule fires on any raw-IP URL regardless of address class, but `127.0.0.1` is the only safe address to bind a local-only server to.
